long_synopsis: Week 72 showed democratic erosion through administration rather than spectacle. Immigration detention became the clearest human story: detainees at Delaney Hall struck over conditions and legal access, reports documented suicides and contaminated food in custody, and oversight narrowed as ICE restricted congressional visits and ended one death-reporting channel. At the same time, the administration expanded coercive immigration power through an asset-seizure order and a Senate enforcement package that enlarged detention and border capacity. Elsewhere, the White House moved to politicize the civil service and public grants, while donor-linked contracts, loans, and prestige projects reinforced a pay-to-play pattern. The Justice Department added to rule-of-law concerns through retaliatory-looking investigations and equivocation about obeying court orders. Courts, cities, and some lawmakers pushed back in meaningful but uneven ways, offsetting the week’s damage without reversing its deeper pattern.
short_synopsis: Week 72 brought no clock movement, but not because conditions stabilized. Detention abuse, politicized staffing, weakened oversight, and donor-linked favoritism advanced, while courts, cities, and Congress supplied enough fragmented resistance to keep the week in near balance.
